source_work: Noah Webster, An American Dictionary of the English Language (1828)
rights_basis: The original 1828 dictionary text is public domain; only its historical definitions and examples are transcribed, not website editorial material.
transcription_source: Internet Archive volume 2 printed page scans and OCR, cross-checked against clean online Webster transcriptions; original OCR is retained unchanged.
selection_method: Selected the first four exact KJV-used T headwords in alphabetical order from the unreviewed high/medium OCR queue. This is a targeted OCR queue, not a claim that all Webster entries have been reviewed.
review_method: Visually checked every sense against the printed page scans and used clean online transcriptions only as secondary aids. Corrected OCR substitutions, scan breaks, column interleaving, page headers, punctuation, and numbering; retained historical examples, usage labels, and author citations. Expanded parts of speech and normalized whitespace for display. Readable etymology is retained while uncertain non-Latin characters are conservatively transliterated rather than guessed. Source spans are one-based lines in the hash-verified OCR file.
review_scope: All definitions and examples: three TAME adjective senses and four transitive senses; eight TEMPER transitive senses and eight noun senses; the THINKING participle, adjective, and noun forms; and the TRADING participle, adjective, and noun forms.

entries.review_note: Scan n733 confirms three adjective senses, four transitive senses, Roscommon, the James iii citation, and the full readable etymology. The base parser omitted the adjective entry and most verb senses after three-column interleaving with TAMPING and TANGLE. Corrected TAMB, wildtiess, getcminn, zahnien, dumar, numbering, and split-the damage; transliterated uncertain Greek and Semitic forms conservatively and excluded TAMED and following entries.

Scan n741 confirms the etymology, eight transitive senses, eight noun senses, all quotations and citations, and the usage note on irritation. The three-column OCR separated the verb heading from its etymology and senses, interleaved TEMPERAMENT and TEMPERANCE, inserted page headers, and merged TEMPERATE into the noun record. Corrected numbering, substitutions, quotations, and punctuation; excluded TEMPERAMENT and following entries.

Scan n758 confirms the participle, adjective, and noun forms and the complete Shakespeare quotation continuing at the top of the next column. Corrected p;7r, siippos iiig, tlie, cogita-tive, ef, Iinaginuliou, missing punctuation, and scan breaks; excluded THINLY and following entries.

Scan n786 confirms the participle, adjective, and noun forms as three short records. Corrected scan-break hyphenation and normalized the printed role marker for display. Replaced the base noun record that swallowed the full neighboring TRADITION entry; TRADITION and later entries are excluded.
